title: Dark-mode interaction ink reflow and graph legend hierarchy
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: In deep-dark console themes interactive elements (buttons, menus, toggles) exhibit visual artifacts and perceived weight due to 'ink' reflow and overlay rules. Chart legends and color keys lose hierarchy against near-black surfaces, and dense tables depend on thin separators that drop below readable contrast at small sizes. Scope: Create a token mapping and component override proposal for deep/dense dark surfaces that preserves accessible contrast, preserves brand accent identity, and avoids visual clutter across tables, charts, and controls. Deliverables: 1) Token transform rules (alpha overlays, elevation-strength multipliers, accent-saturation clamp) 2) Component override spec for Button / Menu / Toggle / Table row / Chart legend 3) Figma tokens and component variants 4) Implementation guidance for theme engine (runtime mapping + opt-in canary) 5) Automated contrast tests and visual regression sets.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New dark token set (overlay-strength, interactive-ink-pressed, accent-legend-contrast, table-separator-visibility) exists in Figma and tokens.json; 2) Component overrides defined with clear fallbacks and examples for three density settings (compact, default, dense); 3) All interactive states meet WCAG AA contrast against their immediate surface for body text and icons; 4) Chart legend examples (categorical and continuous) show preserved brand hue with increased perceived contrast without exceeding saturation clamp; 5) Implementation PR (console-theme) includes unit/storybook examples and a runtime toggle; 6) Canary rollout metrics show no >1% regression in user task success on navigation and no increase in error reports in 72h after rollout.
comments: 2025-02-10 Ava Chen: Initial triage and problem statement added. Observed issues on staging with 'midnight' theme—buttons appear visually heavier on hover due to high overlay alpha. Logged sample screenshots in Figma.

2025-02-12 Diego Morales: Did a quick audit of current token stack. Root cause is a flat conversion from light tokens to dark tokens (invert + mute) causing inconsistent elevation perception. Proposed a layered overlay approach. Assigned to design to spec tokens.
2025-02-14 PM-review (Jordan Patel): Agrees with risk profile; asked to include A/B test plan for canary and to define metric targets for legend readability (time-to-identify color key).

2025-02-16 Design review (Ava/Diego/Celeste): Ran three Figma variants. Decided on overlay-strength=0.18 for primary surfaces and interactive-ink-pressed alpha=0.28 for pressed states. Trade-off: slightly higher perceived ink vs. potential brand accent shift—mitigate with saturation clamp and brand-safe hue remapping.

2025-02-18 Engineering feedback (Liam R.): Runtime mapping is feasible. Suggested adding a feature-flag to enable legacy behavior for Dedicated customers during rollout. Also requested token names be aligned with existing runtime keys (interactive.ink.pressed, overlay.strength, accent.legend.contrast).
2025-02-19 QA (Maya): Started building contrast test harness. Identified two chart palettes where low-saturation hues fail; created remediation palette and added to attachments.
